items.heading: Every Teenager Delays a Hard
items.text: Every teenager delays a hard decision sometimes. Avoidance is different: it is a consistent pattern of dodging the subject itself, regardless of how the question is framed or how much time has passed. This is the signal most parents notice first and misread most often, reading it as laziness or disinterest, when research on career indecision links it more often to anxiety about the decision than to not caring about it.

items.heading: Changing Direction Once or Twice
items.text: Changing direction once or twice is not a red flag. A teenager who hears about a new field, talks to someone doing that work, or tries a short project and updates their thinking afterward is doing exactly what healthy exploration looks like. The signal worth watching for is reversal without new input, going back and forth between the same two or three options repeatedly, with no new fact, conversation, or experience actually driving the change.

items.heading: "I Haven't Thought About IT
items.text: "I haven't thought about it much yet", said once or twice, without tension in the voice.

items.heading: Genuine Engagement When You Bring
items.text: Genuine engagement when you bring up a specific field or option, even if the answer is still "maybe.".

items.heading: Occasional Deflection During a Busy
items.text: Occasional deflection during a busy exam week, that eases once the pressure passes.
